feature: Proactive schema-drift guard — every Drizzle-TS column on the operational error spine actually exists in the live DB (a migration written but never run shows up here BEFORE it dead-letters)
notes: Epic #803. PROACTIVE half of the schema-drift pair (reactive half: observability/dlq-schema-error-scan.json).
Cross-references the Drizzle TypeScript schema (lib/db/src/schema/*.ts) against the real live schema via
information_schema.columns, through #896's read-only POST /admin/deploy/sql-test. Any column TS defines
that is missing live = a migration written but never run.
HONEST SCOPE LIMIT — this is the point the task anticipated. Full automated cross-reference of ALL 259
pgTable() definitions in one manifest step is NOT practical: SQL cannot read the TS files, so the expected
column set has to be embedded as a snapshot, and a hand-embedded 2000+-column snapshot would rot on every
schema change and risk transcription-error FALSE POSITIVES (the worst outcome for trust in a green suite).
So this manifest guards a bounded, accurately-transcribed WATCH-LIST: the operational error spine
(msp_dlq_store lib/db/src/schema/msp.ts:557, msp_job_queue :855, outbound_webhooks :888) — 44 columns —
which is exactly where a never-run migration surfaces as the DLQ errors the reactive half scans for.
The FULL periodic sweep across the rest of the schema is the standalone diagnostic Shane runs by hand:
lib/db/migrations/manual/archive/diagnostics/2026-08-13-schema-drift-ts-vs-live.sql (which also carries the
recipe to regenerate/extend the expected VALUES list from the TS schema). This split is deliberate, not
faked coverage.
Two assertions make the guard non-vacuous:
1. drift query — LEFT JOIN, returns any watch-listed (table,column) MISSING live; asserts $.rowCount==0,
and $.rows names the exact missing table/column on failure.
2. presence count — inner JOIN counts how many of the 44 watch-listed columns ARE present live; asserts
it equals 44. This catches a whole table/column vanishing (which would make assertion 1 pass vacuously)
and is intentionally NOT brittle to columns being ADDED later (an inner join only counts the expected set).
count(*) is cast ::int so node-postgres returns a JSON number (bigint would serialize as a string '44').
Queries are written SELECT-first (VALUES inlined as a FROM-subquery, NOT a leading WITH/CTE) because the
sql-test validator only accepts statements beginning with SELECT (admin-deploy-console.ts:273). Read-only,
single statement, no forbidden write/DDL keyword. NOT live-verified from this environment (no DB access —
CLAUDE.md); the runner / Shane executes it. When a spine column is legitimately added in TS + migrated, bump
the VALUES list AND the presence-count expected value (44) together, and update lastVerifiedAgainstCommit.
